Publication: THE FIELD NOTES
Title: What we learned from a year of four-day weeks
Byline: By Maya Ortiz · March 4, 2026 · 7 min read
Body, in order:
1. Last March we tried something our board called “brave” and our accountant called “unwise”: every team would work Monday to Thursday, with Friday off and no cut in pay. We promised to measure everything and to stop if it didn’t work.
2. We expected output to fall. Instead, most teams shipped slightly more, and the number of late projects dropped by a third. The biggest change was not speed but focus: people stopped filling Fridays with meetings that could have been an email.
3. Pull quote: “I get more done in four focused days than I used to in five scattered ones.”
4. That line came from our support lead, and it summed up the survey.
5. Key sentence (the one to stress): Nobody wanted to go back.
6. Even the two teams whose numbers dipped asked to keep the schedule and fix the problems instead.

Title: The Quiet Return of the Night Train
Byline: By Hannah Okafor · November 9, 2026 · 8 min read
Body:
1. Ten years ago, the sleeper train looked finished. Budget airlines had taken the routes, the carriages were old, and operators were cutting services every winter. Today new lines open every season, and many of them sell out weeks in advance.
2. What changed was not the trains themselves but the travellers. Families, remote workers and people avoiding short flights now treat a night on the rails as part of the trip rather than a cost of it.
Pull quote: "You go to sleep in one country and wake up in another. No airport has ever given me that."
Figure: years 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026; caption: Figure 1. Night train routes in Europe, 2020 to 2026. Source: Rail Europe Watch.

Section: Checking the timetable yourself
Text: Most operators publish their timetables as open data. A short query is enough to find every overnight departure:
Code (SQL):
SELECT route, depart, arrive
FROM departures
WHERE depart >= '20:00'
AND overnight = true
ORDER BY depart;

- Book as soon as the season opens, usually ninety days ahead.
- Choose a lower berth if you want an easy climb at night.

- Check whether breakfast is included before you pay extra.

- 38%: fewer abandoned checkouts

challenges.content:
Category: Sunday dinner
Recipe: Lemon and Herb Roast Chicken
Description: A whole chicken roasted over sliced lemons and garlic, with crisp golden skin and juices that make their own sauce.
Facts (label: value):
Time: 1 hr 30 min
Serves: 4
Difficulty: Easy
Ingredients:
- 1 whole chicken, about 1.6 kg
- 2 unwaxed lemons
- 1 head of garlic
- 4 sprigs of thyme
- 2 sprigs of rosemary
- 40 g soft butter
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 150 ml chicken stock
- Sea salt and black pepper
Method:
1. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking.
2. Slice one lemon and halve the garlic head across. Lay them in a roasting tin with half the herbs.
3. Mix the butter with the zest of the second lemon, the leaves from the remaining thyme and a good pinch of salt.
4. Loosen the skin over the breast and push the butter underneath. Put the zested lemon inside the bird.
5. Sit the chicken on the lemons, rub with olive oil and season. Roast for 1 hr 15 min, basting halfway.
6. Rest the chicken for 15 minutes. Add the stock to the tin, scrape up the juices and simmer for 3 minutes.
Cook's tip: The chicken is done when the juices run clear from the thickest part of the thigh, or a probe reads 75°C.
